paragraphs.en: All around the world, lawyers generate more hostility than the members of any other profession – with the possible exception of journalism. But there are few places where clients have more grounds for complaint than America.
paragraphs.zh: 在世界各地，律师招致的敌意都比其他任何职业的人更多，新闻从业者可能是唯一的例外。但很少有哪个地方的客户，像美国客户这样有充分的理由抱怨。

paragraphs.en: During the decade before the economic crisis, spending on legal services in America grew twice as fast as inflation. The best lawyers made skyscrapers-full of money, tempting ever more students to pile into law schools. But most law graduates never get a big-firm job. Many of them instead become the kind of nuisance-lawsuit filer that makes the tort system a costly nightmare.
paragraphs.zh: 在经济危机之前的十年里，美国法律服务支出的增长速度，是通货膨胀率的两倍。最优秀的律师赚得盆满钵满，诱使越来越多的学生涌入法学院。但大多数法学院毕业生从未得到过大律所的工作。他们中的许多人反而成了那种专门提起滋扰性诉讼的人，使侵权诉讼制度变成代价高昂的噩梦。

paragraphs.en: There are many reasons for this. One is the excessive costs of a legal education. There is just one path for a lawyer in most American states: a four-year undergraduate degree in some unrelated subject, then a three-year law degree at one of 200 law schools authorized by the American Bar Association and an expensive preparation for the bar exam. This leaves today’s average law-school graduate with $100,000 of debt on top of undergraduate debts. Law-school debt means that they have to work fearsomely hard.
paragraphs.zh: 造成这种情况有许多原因。其中之一，是法学教育费用过高。在美国大多数州，成为律师只有一条路：先用四年时间取得某个无关专业的本科学位，再到美国律师协会认可的二百所法学院之一，攻读三年的法学学位，然后花费高昂费用准备律师资格考试。这使得如今的法学院毕业生，除了本科阶段的债务之外，平均还背负着十万美元的债务。法学院欠下的债务，意味着他们不得不拼命工作。

paragraphs.en: Reforming the system would help both lawyers and their customers. Sensible ideas have been around for a long time, but the state-level bodies that govern the profession have been too conservative to implement them. One idea is to allow people to study law as an undergraduate degree. Another is to let students sit for the bar after only two years of law school. If the bar exam is truly a stern enough test for a would-be lawyer, those who can sit it earlier should be allowed to do so. Students who do not need the extra training could cut their debt mountain by a third.
paragraphs.zh: 改革这一制度，对律师和客户都有帮助。合理的建议早已存在，但州一级的行业管理机构过于保守，迟迟不愿实施。一种建议是允许人们在本科阶段学习法律，取得法学学士学位。另一种建议是允许学生在法学院学习两年后，就参加律师资格考试。如果律师资格考试对未来律师而言确实足够严格，那么那些有能力提前应试的人，就应当获准这样做。无需额外培训的学生，就可以将自己沉重的债务减少三分之一。

paragraphs.en: The other reason why costs are so high is the restrictive guild-like ownership structure of the business. Except in the District of Columbia, non-lawyers may not own any share of a law firm. This keeps fees high and innovation slow. There is pressure for change from within the profession, but opponents of change among the regulators insist that keeping outsiders out of a law firm isolates lawyers from the pressure to make money rather than serve clients ethically.
paragraphs.zh: 费用如此高昂的另一个原因，是这一行业存在类似行会、限制严格的所有权结构。除哥伦比亚特区之外，非律师不得拥有律师事务所的任何股份。这使收费居高不下，创新进展缓慢。行业内部存在要求改革的压力，但监管者中的反对派坚称，将外行拒之于律所门外，能让律师免受赚钱压力的影响，从而不至于牺牲合乎职业道德的客户服务。

paragraphs.en: In fact, allowing non-lawyers to own shares in law firms would reduce costs and improve services to customers, by encouraging law firms to use technology and to employ professional managers to focus on improving firms’ efficiency. After all, other countries, such as Australia and Britain, have started liberalizing their legal professions. America should follow.
paragraphs.zh: 实际上，允许非律师持有律所股份，会鼓励律所使用技术，并雇用专业经理人专注于提高效率，从而降低成本、改善对客户的服务。毕竟，澳大利亚和英国等其他国家，已经开始放宽对法律行业的限制。美国也应该跟进。
